content.text: {"relation": "DIVERGENT", "consensus_summary": "The blind consensus treats the new moon as the observance marking the beginning of the lunar month (understood astronomically as the dark conjunction or first visible crescent), whose Christian symbolic significance is primarily that of a ceremonial 'shadow' fulfilled in Christ (Col 2:16-17), with secondary associations of renewal/new beginnings, prophetic critique of empty ritual, and eschatological perpetual worship (Isa 66:23).", "book_summary": "The book defines the 'new moon' as the renewed moon — but identifies the phase that begins the month as the FULL moon, associated with the opened east gate (Ezek 46) and functioning as the sign of the appointed times. It explicitly flags and rejects the commonly taught identification with the dark conjunction or first visible crescent.", "consensus_core_identification": "The new moon is the start-of-month observance occurring at the dark/crescent phase, functioning as part of Israel's ceremonial calendar and, in Christian reading, as a shadow pointing to Christ.", "book_core_identification": "The new moon is the full moon, which is the true phase that begins the month and serves as the sign of God's appointed times (linked to the east-gate worship of Ezekiel 46).", "core_relation": "CONTRADICTS", "extension_relation": "DIFFERENT_REFERENT", "boundary_disagreement": "The disagreement is not about which occasions are ceremonially significant but about which astronomical event the term denotes: the book relocates the 'new moon' from the dark conjunction/first crescent to the full moon, thereby moving the month's start to a different day and a different observable phenomenon.", "material_contradiction": "The book asserts the month begins at the full moon; the common teaching (which all consensus responses presuppose) holds it begins at the dark conjunction or first visible crescent. Both cannot be true of the same term in the same calendrical sense, and the book's own common-view note explicitly denies the standard identification.", "rationale": "Both axes must be judged. On the symbolic/functional axis, the book overlaps with consensus (a marker of appointed times, tied to worship and Col 2:16-17's framework). But the book's central identification is astronomical-calendrical: 'new moon' = full moon. This is a replacement of the referent rather than a boundary refinement — accepting the book requires rejecting the phase identification implicit in every consensus response and explicitly named in the book's common-view note. The consensus's shared cases (Ps 81:3, 1 Sam 20, Isa 66:23, Ezek 46) are retained but reassigned to a different astronomical event, which fits DIVERGENT with DIFFERENT_REFERENT despite overlapping textual extension.", "citation_support": "PARTIAL", "strongest_objection": "One could argue the consensus responses addressed symbolic meaning, not lunar astronomy, so the book's full-moon claim is orthogonal and should be NOVEL rather than DIVERGENT; the book still agrees the day marks the month's start and is a shadow/sign, preserving the consensus category. However, the book's explicit denial of the commonly taught phase makes this a contradiction of the shared baseline referent, not a mere absence from it.", "confidence": "high"}
